source.revision_label: main head 2026-08-01, 'Add BindCraft-style optimizer (#73)'; the repository publishes no git tags

required_environment.FS2_ARTIFACT_ROOT: root of the external artifact plane; defaults to /opt/fs2/artifacts
required_environment.FS2_INPUT_ARTIFACT_ROOT: root containing controller-materialized request artifacts; defaults to FS2_ARTIFACT_ROOT for backward-compatible direct runs
required_environment.FS2_RUNTIME_IMAGE_DIGEST: aggregate stage only; binds the committed manifest to the admitted image digest

accelerator_runtime.architecture_policy: the JAX CUDA 12 plugin discovers NVIDIA GPUs dynamically; no device-name or H100-only admission check. Upstream-pinned CPU PyTorch 2.7.1 is retained solely for checkpoint conversion.

supersedes.reason: H100 semantic-qualified for the historical one-root Job, but it cannot read controller-materialized request bytes separately from the immutable model-artifact root. The v6 successor adds that production split-root contract; evidence does not transfer across image digests.
pre-qualification adapter wiring; never reached a real H100 semantic forward

completed a real H100 Boltz-2/ProteinMPNN forward but serialised the binder structure with Gemmi UNK residue names, so the designed sequence could not be recovered from the PDB. Both the canonical adapter output validator and the qualification validator reject it.

corrected the binder PDB residue naming but kept image cache defaults under the image filesystem and the read-only artifact plane. Under the canonical readOnlyRootFilesystem Job, Boltz aborts at import with numba 'cannot cache function _prepare_msa_arrays_inner: no locator available'. Observed live on H100 job mosaic-4d5fd258d1ceec2c-s000, exit code 1.

first image that survives the canonical readOnlyRootFilesystem Job, but it was built from the pre-fix entrypoint that serialises the binder chain straight from Gemmi, so every residue is still named UNK and the designed sequence is unrecoverable.

cache_policy.rationale: the canonical Job mounts only the request ConfigMap, /workspace and a /tmp emptyDir and sets readOnlyRootFilesystem, so every cache default must resolve under /tmp

qualification.evidence_transfer_policy: The adapter-v6 split-root receipt is first-party evidence for the exact successor digest. Historical adapter-v5 evidence remains only as the independently reproduced semantic baseline; route exposure still requires the serialized production-controller run.
qualification.scope: adapter-v6 is semantically qualified on H100 for the bounded design and aggregate workflow with canonical model and request bytes on separate read-only roots; no production-controller, throughput, GPU snapshot, elasticity, contention, or other accelerator-family claim is made

weight_policy.notes: Upstream ships three ProteinMPNN checkpoints inside the package tree. They are deleted before installation so the image carries no model bytes; every component checkpoint is mounted from the external artifact plane.

external_artifacts.notes: Boltz-2 reads canonical molecules from the extracted mols/ directory; the Boltz-1 ccd.pkl path is not part of this contract.

artifact_delivery.detail: The canonical regional artifact plane now publishes every Mosaic model byte as an accepted content-addressed generation on the public reference-data host plane, and a real H100 run has consumed them. The transitional copy on the shared qualification claim is retained only as an archival record of the original semantic run and is no longer a delivery path. Because the runtime resolves each checkpoint by SHA-256, the binding needed no image change, exactly as this lock predicted.

canonical_generations.note: This lock's boltz2-mols entry pins the Boltz-2 mols.tar archive. That archive and BoltzGen's mols.zip expand to one identical flat tree, proven entry by entry on 2026-09-04, so Mosaic binds the already-published generation instead of a duplicate identity. Evidence: models/cancer-immunotherapy/artifact-localization/evidence/mosaic-molecule-tree-equivalence-20260904.json.
All three upstream ProteinMPNN checkpoints are localized as one indivisible weights directory. The r12 runtime reads only v_48_020.pt today.

artifact_delivery.mount_composition: The runtime resolves three fixed locations under FS2_ARTIFACT_ROOT and they are three separate generations, so the checkpoint is bound as a single file and its two siblings as directories. The intermediate mosaic/boltz directory is created by the kubelet and is never itself a mount, which is what lets a file and a directory sit beside each other without either nesting inside the other's read-only mount.

upstream_contract_defects.actual: models/bionemo/boltz2/artifact-manifest.json hashes to 6e837710a2a1dd619d1a5405eba98cafcb529cc36d180e4469c138c54aa2dfe3, identically at 6551d870, at main c83b97c6 and at the integration base main b77ccfa7
upstream_contract_defects.impact: any consumer that verifies the referenced manifest by its pinned digest fails closed. The referenced content digest 9459dd0c... and the checkpoint digest 090e82ac... are correct, so this is a stale pin on the pointer, not on the artifact.
upstream_contract_defects.resolution: reported to the primary adapter owner; this runtime verifies the checkpoint and molecule identities directly and does not consume the stale manifest pin.
upstream_contract_defects.reconfirmed_at: 0bdfc244; still stale in the adapter candidate

upstream_contract_defects.observed: the rendered aggregate Job carries no container env and no --runtime-image-digest argument
upstream_contract_defects.actual: validate_output_manifest requires aggregate.runtime_image_digest to equal the admitted runtime image digest
upstream_contract_defects.impact: a plan rendered strictly by the canonical adapter can never produce an aggregate the canonical validator accepts
upstream_contract_defects.resolution: reported to the primary adapter owner. This runtime reads FS2_RUNTIME_IMAGE_DIGEST and fails closed when it is absent, so the adapter only has to project the admitted digest into the aggregate Job env.

upstream_contract_defects.observed: readOnlyRootFilesystem: true with only a ConfigMap, /workspace and /tmp emptyDir mounted, and no container env
upstream_contract_defects.actual: Boltz decorates its MSA featuriser with numba @njit(cache=True), which requires a writable cache locator; JAX, Hugging Face and Matplotlib also default to caches under HOME
upstream_contract_defects.impact: a strictly canonical Job aborts at import before any GPU work
upstream_contract_defects.resolution: the image now defaults every cache under /tmp, which the canonical Job always provides. No change to the adapter is required for this defect.

preserved: mosaic image inputs and the canonical mosaic-batch wrapper binding
immutable digest lock and the superseded-publication chain
H100 semantic evidence and the canonical-plan qualification tooling
integration.not_replayed: no adapter, controller, catalog, admin, Terraform or shared-service file is touched; the canonical adapter stays owned by its own task and is only read from commit 6551d870

catalog_constants.canonical_bytes_encoding: sorted keys, compact separators, ASCII, trailing newline; identical to the runtime encoding

artifact_contract_reconciliation.canonical_mosaic_artifact_root: still absent on main, so artifact delivery remains transitional-task-scoped
artifact_contract_reconciliation.conclusion: the stale pin is in the adapter candidate, not in the artifact plane. The referenced manifest, its content digest and both component identities are correct and unchanged at the integration base, so this runtime keeps verifying the checkpoint and molecule identities directly and never consumes the stale pointer pin.

blocker_handoff.scope: three of the four recorded defects need an adapter or plan-renderer change; this task does not edit controller or adapter ownership

closed_here.detail: Closed for the canonical path by qualification/adapt_canonical.py, which binds every accepted generation read-only at the exact path the immutable runtime reads, reads each generation digest out of the localization contract rather than accepting it from the command line, and admits each in-generation marker in the consuming pod. The canonical batch adapter itself still renders no artifact mount, so the adapter owner's change is still needed for controller-driven runs.

follow_ups.observed: The canonical plan sets pod fsGroup 10001 and mounts the shared run claim, so the kubelet chowns the whole claim before any container starts. Observed live on 2026-09-04: VolumePermissionChangeInProgress for 92 s, 51,679 files processed, delaying the marker admission and the GPU stage by about two minutes.
follow_ups.proposal: Set fsGroupChangePolicy OnRootMismatch on the plan's pod security context, or give the run claim its own per-run subdirectory. The read-only generation mounts are not affected because the kubelet does not chown a read-only bind mount.

follow_ups.observed: The contract's consumer model pairs one binding name with one mount path, and the receipt reports the mount path as the binding value. Mosaic has no per-artifact lever: the runtime derives three fixed sub-paths from a single FS2_ARTIFACT_ROOT, so each of the three consumers has to name FS2_ARTIFACT_ROOT while its recorded binding value is the resolved mount rather than the root itself.
follow_ups.impact: A reader of the receipt alone could take the binding value for the environment variable's value. The entries' notes state the exact resolution rule, but the shape cannot express it.
follow_ups.proposal: Allow a consumer to declare a root binding plus a relative path, for example binding_name FS2_ARTIFACT_ROOT with binding_root /opt/fs2/artifacts and binding_relative_path mosaic/boltz/mols, so the receipt can report both.

follow_ups.observed: generation_marker projects tree.mount_paths into the generation's consumer_paths, and the marker is sealed inside the generation and immutable once published. Adding a second mount path to an already-published artifact therefore changes the marker digest the contract expects while the marker on the plane keeps the old one, so a strict admission that pins --expect-manifest-digest fails against bytes that are perfectly valid.
follow_ups.impact: A new consumer of an existing generation cannot declare its own mount without either republishing the generation or weakening admission. Observed on 2026-09-04 when Mosaic was given a second mount on boltzgen-inference-molecules: the expected marker digest moved from 7f0e2c401abd73c1d4ff6deb6719e027db6ee9a75f7b7ed940b1e63ff54bbae4 to 19b676f959acb6187978c663daa6ea0a21d8078279d8317ad9227cdb098bac91.
follow_ups.resolution: Mosaic's consumer declares the artifact's existing mount and its Job binds the same content-addressed generation at the path the immutable runtime reads. The durable fix is to keep consumer paths out of the marker, since they describe how a tree is consumed rather than what it contains, and the marker's job is to identify content.
